views.back: Behind the baseline, roughly centred, camera at 0.5-2 m: the app's target view
views.back_corner: Behind the baseline near a corner, looking diagonally (about 20-50 degrees off the court axis)
views.side: Level with the player, beside the court, looking across it
views.front: Facing the player (from the net or the far side)
views.elevated: Camera above 3 m (stands, broadcast, top-down); judge body checkpoints only when the player is large and clear

view_ratings.limited: judge only when it is obvious; otherwise cant_tell

special_values.cant_tell: Visible stroke, but this checkpoint cannot be judged from this footage
special_values.not_applicable: Checkpoint doesn't apply to this particular ball (e.g. no opponent swing for split_step)

clip_fields.definition: Licence of the footage (e.g. CC BY-NC 4.0)
Same value for clips filmed at the same moment by different cameras
Stable id per person across clips (needed for player-level splits)

stroke_fields.definition: The stroke actually played (correct the detector's suggestion if needed).
Optional refinement of the stroke type.
How the ball arrived; 'shadow' = no ball.
yes = whole body visible through the stroke; partial = some joints hidden/cut off or blurred; no = skip.
Can you see the ball around contact?
Bounce depth on the far side.
1 = breaks down (major faults); 2 = several clear faults; 3 = functional with one or two faults; 4 = solid, minor issues; 5 = textbook for this player's level of ball.
How good this stroke looks, ignoring who the player is.
If a coach could fix one thing, which checkpoint? Must be one marked as a fault on this stroke.

groundstroke.definition: First frame the shoulders/racket start turning back
Ball bounce on the player's side (if visible)
Racket furthest back, just before the forward swing
Racket at the end of the follow-through

volley.definition: Feet land from the split step

serve.definition: Tossing arm highest / racket up, knees most bent
Racket at its lowest point behind the back

smash.definition: Racket at its lowest point behind the back

checkpoints.name: Split step
checkpoints.question: Does the player do a small hop / split step as the opponent strikes the ball?

options.definition: Both feet leave or unweight the ground as the opponent hits
Split step happens clearly after the opponent's contact
No split step; flat-footed or already running

checkpoints.notes: Skip (cant_tell) on fed balls where there is no opponent swing.

checkpoints.name: Early preparation
checkpoints.moment: ball bounce on the player's side
checkpoints.question: When the ball bounces, have the shoulders and racket already turned back?

options.definition: Turn complete before the bounce
Turn finishing around the bounce
Still turning (or not started) after the bounce; rushed swing

checkpoints.name: Shoulder turn
checkpoints.question: How far have the shoulders turned away from the net at the end of the backswing?

options.definition: Shoulder line at least perpendicular to the net (points at the net); back partly turned to the net
Roughly halfway (about 45 degrees)
Chest still mostly facing the net; arm-only takeback

checkpoints.name: Non-hitting arm in the turn
checkpoints.question: Does the non-hitting arm extend across in front of the body during the turn?

options.definition: Arm reaches across, roughly parallel to the baseline, helping the turn
Arm lifts but stays bent close to the body
Arm hangs or stays tucked; does not take part in the turn

checkpoints.name: Size of takeback
checkpoints.question: How big is the backswing?

options.definition: Racket goes back to around the back shoulder / side fence line
Racket goes clearly past the back shoulder
Racket wraps far behind the back; a long, late loop

checkpoints.name: Racket drops below the ball
checkpoints.question: Just before the forward swing, is the racket head below the height where contact happens?

options.definition: Racket head clearly below contact height (sets up low-to-high)
About level with contact height
Racket stays above contact height and swings down or flat

checkpoints.name: Knee bend (loading)
checkpoints.moment: end of backswing / just before contact for volleys
checkpoints.question: How bent are the legs while loading?

options.definition: Clear knee bend, hips lowered (an athletic 'sit')
Small bend
Legs nearly straight; standing tall

checkpoints.name: Stance
checkpoints.question: What stance is the player in at contact? (Descriptive; not a fault by itself.)

options.definition: Feet roughly parallel to the baseline
Between open and neutral
Front foot stepped forward; feet roughly along the court
Front foot stepped across beyond the back foot

checkpoints.notes: Descriptor: use it to interpret other checkpoints (e.g. rotation is expected to differ by stance).

checkpoints.name: Contact in front
checkpoints.question: Along the direction of the court, where is the ball met relative to the body?

options.definition: Ahead of the front hip (serve: ahead of the head/body, into the court)
Level with the body
Behind the body (serve/smash: behind the head)

checkpoints.notes: From directly behind or in front this is a depth judgement; mark cant_tell unless it is obvious.

checkpoints.name: Spacing from the ball
checkpoints.question: Sideways, how far from the body is the ball met?

options.definition: Ball too close; elbow jammed against the body
Comfortable arm's-length space
Ball too far; lunging or reaching with a straight, stretched arm

checkpoints.name: Contact height
checkpoints.question: At what height is the ball met? (Descriptive; the right height depends on the ball.)

options.definition: Below the knee
Knee to waist
Waist to chest (the comfortable zone)
Above the shoulder

checkpoints.name: Hitting arm at contact
checkpoints.question: How is the hitting arm shaped at contact?

options.definition: Nearly straight
Clearly bent at the elbow but with space from the body
Elbow tucked into the body

checkpoints.notes: For one-handed backhands a straight arm is expected; mark 'bent' as a fault in analysis, not here.

checkpoints.name: Both hands through contact
checkpoints.question: Do both hands stay on the racket through contact?

options.definition: Both hands on the grip until after contact
Top hand comes off before or at contact

checkpoints.name: Rotation through contact
checkpoints.question: Do the hips and shoulders rotate forward through contact?

options.definition: Chest turns to face the net by or just after contact
Some rotation, stops short
Body stays still; the arm does the work

checkpoints.notes: One-handed backhands and slices use shoulders_stay_sideways instead.

checkpoints.name: Shoulders stay sideways
checkpoints.question: Do the shoulders stay side-on (not opening up) through contact?

options.definition: Shoulders still roughly perpendicular to the net at contact
Chest swings open to the net before contact

checkpoints.name: Head steady
checkpoints.question: Does the head stay still and facing the contact zone through contact?

options.definition: Head steady; still pointed at the contact zone just after contact
Head jerks up or turns to look at the target before or at contact

checkpoints.name: Balance at contact
checkpoints.question: Is the upper body balanced at contact?

options.definition: Trunk upright or leaning naturally into the shot
Falling or leaning away from the ball / backwards
Toppling sideways

checkpoints.name: Weight transfer
checkpoints.question: Is the body weight moving forward into the ball?

options.definition: Weight moving forward / into the court
Stationary
Moving away from the ball or back

checkpoints.name: Low-to-high swing
checkpoints.question: What is the racket path through the ball?

options.definition: Clearly rises through contact
Mostly level
Comes down through the ball (unintended slice/chop)

checkpoints.name: Finish position
checkpoints.question: Where does the racket finish?

options.definition: Over the opposite shoulder (two-hander: over the shoulder; one-hander: high, arm extended toward target)
Around the neck/body at shoulder height
Low across the body (windshield-wiper finish)
Swing stops soon after contact

checkpoints.notes: 'low_across' is a legitimate modern variation; only 'stops_short' is a fault.

checkpoints.name: Balance at finish
checkpoints.question: Is the player balanced after the shot?

options.definition: Holds the finish / recovers without stumbling
Needs an extra step to catch balance
Clearly off balance

checkpoints.name: Recovery
checkpoints.question: Does the player recover toward a ready position for the next ball?

options.definition: Moves back toward the middle / ready position
Stays to watch the shot

checkpoints.name: High takeback (slice)
checkpoints.question: Does the racket start above the height of contact?

options.definition: Racket starts clearly above contact height
Starts about level
Starts below contact height

checkpoints.name: Slice swing path
checkpoints.question: What is the racket path through the ball?

options.definition: Moves down and forward through the ball
Steep downward chop with little forward movement
Level or rising path

checkpoints.name: Racket face (slice)
checkpoints.question: Is the racket face open (tilted back) at contact?

options.definition: Face tilted back slightly
Face vertical
Face tilted far back (floats the ball)

checkpoints.notes: Needs a clear, close view of the racket; mark cant_tell otherwise.

checkpoints.name: Slice finish
checkpoints.question: Where does the racket finish?

options.definition: Extends forward toward the target, arm long
Wraps around the body
Stops right after contact

checkpoints.name: Volley backswing
checkpoints.question: How big is the backswing?

options.definition: Racket stays in front of the body; little or no backswing
Small takeback to about the shoulder
Full swing

checkpoints.name: Step into the volley
checkpoints.question: Does the player step forward into the volley with the opposite foot?

options.definition: Steps forward with the foot opposite the hitting side
Steps with the same-side foot
No forward step

checkpoints.name: Racket head up
checkpoints.question: At contact, is the racket head above the wrist?

options.definition: Racket head above the wrist
About level
Racket head drooping below the wrist (on a ball above the knee)

checkpoints.name: Volley follow-through
checkpoints.question: How long is the follow-through?

options.definition: Short, firm punch toward the target
Long swinging finish

checkpoints.name: Serve stance
checkpoints.question: Which stance? (Descriptive.)

options.definition: Feet stay apart through the motion
Back foot slides up next to the front foot

checkpoints.name: Tossing arm
checkpoints.question: Is the tossing arm straight as it releases the ball?

options.definition: Arm long and straight, lifting from the shoulder
Some elbow bend
Elbow clearly bent; flicked toss

checkpoints.name: Toss placement
checkpoints.question: Where is the toss relative to the body?

options.definition: Slightly in front and toward the hitting side
Straight above the head
Behind the head
Far out to either side

checkpoints.notes: From behind you can judge left/right well but in front/behind poorly; from the side the reverse.

checkpoints.name: Toss height
checkpoints.question: How high is the toss compared with the reach at contact?

options.definition: Player has to rush or hit with a bent arm
Peaks around or a little above full reach
Ball falls well past the contact point; long wait

checkpoints.name: Trophy position
checkpoints.question: At the trophy position: hitting elbow about shoulder height, racket up, tossing arm pointing up?

options.definition: All three present
One element missing (e.g. elbow low or tossing arm already dropped)
No recognisable trophy position

checkpoints.name: Knee bend at trophy
checkpoints.question: How much do the knees bend in the loading phase?

options.definition: Clear bend
Some bend
Legs straight

checkpoints.name: Shoulder tilt
checkpoints.question: Is the tossing shoulder higher than the hitting shoulder at the trophy?

options.definition: Tossing shoulder clearly higher
Slightly higher
Shoulders level

checkpoints.name: Racket drop
checkpoints.moment: lowest racket position behind the back
checkpoints.question: Does the racket drop down behind the back before swinging up?

options.definition: Racket head points toward the ground behind the back
Racket drops to about shoulder level
Racket pushed forward from the trophy ('waiter's tray' / pushing)

checkpoints.name: Leg drive
checkpoints.question: Do the legs drive up into the ball?

options.definition: Strong extension; feet leave the ground
Legs extend but stay grounded
No push from the legs

checkpoints.name: Reach at contact
checkpoints.question: Is the ball hit at full reach?

options.definition: Hitting arm and body extended up; ball at the highest comfortable point
Arm a little bent or body a little crouched
Clearly below full reach

checkpoints.name: Tossing arm tuck
checkpoints.question: Does the tossing arm pull down and in toward the body as the racket swings up?

options.definition: Arm pulls down into the chest/stomach
Arm falls well before the swing
Arm stays up or flails out

checkpoints.name: Pronation
checkpoints.question: Does the forearm rotate the racket face outward after contact (thumb turning down)?

options.definition: Clear outward rotation
Racket face stays facing forward / wrist slaps down

checkpoints.notes: Needs 60 fps and a close view; usually cant_tell.

checkpoints.name: Landing
checkpoints.question: How does the player land?

options.definition: Lands on the front foot, moving into the court
Lands on both feet behind or at the baseline
Stumbles or lands sideways

checkpoints.name: Serve follow-through
checkpoints.question: Where does the racket finish?

options.definition: Finishes past the body on the non-hitting side
Finishes on the hitting side
Stops in front of the body

checkpoints.name: Rhythm
checkpoints.question: Is the motion continuous?

options.definition: One continuous motion from toss to contact
Clear pause (e.g. at the trophy) that breaks the chain
Hurried; toss and swing out of sync

checkpoints.name: Sideways turn (smash)
checkpoints.question: Does the player turn sideways early, hitting shoulder back?

options.definition: Turns as soon as the lob is recognised
Turns late
Stays facing the net

checkpoints.name: Pointing arm (smash)
checkpoints.question: Does the non-hitting arm point up at the ball?

options.definition: Arm up, tracking the ball
Arm down or not tracking

checkpoints.name: Moving under the ball
checkpoints.question: How does the player move to the ball?

options.definition: Side-steps or crossover steps, staying sideways
Runs backwards facing the net
Does not adjust; reaches for the ball
